title: Failover quorum lag and soft-circuit interaction — incident report and remediation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: On 2026-02-08 we observed a multi-region disruption that produced an SLO miss for 11 minutes across multiple customers. The incident combined a control-plane quorum lag during a rolling maintenance window with 'soft' circuit-breaker behavior that allowed staggered region failover traffic to overwhelm a secondary region's KV-cache warmup capacity, producing cascading backpressure and aggressive load-shedding. This document captures the timeline, root causes, immediate mitigations, and an action plan to prevent recurrence.
impact: 11 minute SLO miss for 7 regional clusters; ~12% tail-latency degradation for latency-sensitive hosted API customers; four enterprise customers reported degraded quality of service and raised P0 support tickets. Estimated revenue-exposed requests: ~1.2M tokens during the window.
timeline: 2026-02-08T01:12Z: Scheduled control-plane rolling maintenance started in primary region (us-west-2).
2026-02-08T01:18Z: Control-plane nodes in two availability zones experienced increased GC and leadership re-election; quorum lag detected by control-plane health monitors.

2026-02-08T01:19Z: Smart routing observed control-plane inconsistency and initiated incremental region failover to secondary (us-east-1) per policy. Traffic fanout increased by ~3x to us-east-1 within 30s.
2026-02-08T01:20Z: Circuit breaker subsystem (soft thresholds) started tripping per-connectivity but used staggered backoff windows; not all proxies transitioned to full-blocking in lockstep.
2026-02-08T01:21Z: KV cache hit-rates in us-east-1 dropped from 89% to 12% as cold traffic populated caches, causing increased GPU memory pressure and higher per-request latency.
2026-02-08T01:23Z: Autoscaler reacted to increased queue length but configured cooldown prevented immediate capacity ramp; burst capacity limits prevented full scale-up.
2026-02-08T01:24Z: Observability alerts triggered (SLO breach), on-call paged; mitigation playbooks started.

2026-02-08T01:25Z: Emergency runbook executed: 1) throttled new onboarding traffic to us-east-1, 2) temporarily widened circuit-breaker thresholds to allow controlled gradation, 3) enabled cross-region cache prewarm for prioritized prefixes.
2026-02-08T01:30Z: Warmup reduced tail latency and hit rates stabilized; traffic slowly rebalanced and SLOs recovered by 01:40Z.
reproduction_steps: 1) In staging, trigger a simulated control-plane leadership churn in primary region while simultaneously shifting routing to secondary region.
2) Configure circuit-breakers to use current production 'soft' staggered backoff windows to reproduce non-lockstep behavior.
3) Send synthetic traffic with realistic prompt distributions to measure KV cache cold-start behavior and autoscaler cooldown effects.
4) Observe queue lengths, per-replica latency, and token throughput; verify SLO violation surfaces when warmup is constrained and autoscaler cooldown prevents immediate scale-up.
root_cause: Control-plane quorum lag during maintenance caused smart routing to initiate rapid incremental region failover.

Circuit-breaker soft (staggered) thresholds led to non-deterministic, partially-open states across proxies; some proxies continued sending full traffic while others limited, creating uneven load redistribution.
KV-cache cold-start at the secondary region and conservative autoscaler cooldowns prevented immediate capacity absorption of failover traffic.
Burst capacity hard limits and lack of emergency prewarm policy for prioritized prefixes amplified tail latency under sudden fanout.
contributing_factors: Maintenance window overlapped with moderate global traffic peak, increasing sensitivity to reconfiguration latency.
Insufficient observability for cross-service warmup (no composite metric linking region routing spikes to per-shard cache-fill progress).
Circuit-breaker hysteresis intentionally tuned to reduce flapping but produced misaligned transition timing across proxies.
Runbook lacked a pre-authorized emergency reserve capacity play to bypass reserved-burst quotas for short windows.
mitigation_taken: Applied emergency throttling for non-enterprise routes to limit additional pressure on us-east-1.
Temporarily widened circuit-breaker thresholds uniformly from 60s to 180s to force consistent behavior across proxies (manual change).
Triggered manual cross-region cache prewarm for top 50 prefixes for affected clusters.
Raised immediate autoscaler target and manually provisioned one extra GPU shard in us-east-1 to alleviate queueing.
long_term_fix_proposals: Introduce control-plane graceful maintenance protocol: stagger maintenance epochs with explicit routing handoff acknowledgement to avoid simultaneous leader churn and routing decisions.
Refactor circuit-breaker implementation to include a coordinated consensus step for threshold transitions (soft->open) to avoid skirted partial states across proxies.
Implement prioritized KV-cache proactive prewarm on failover signal for top N prefixes and enterprise routes with a fast-path prefill mechanism from snapshot stores.
Adjust autoscaler cooldown heuristics to allow short-duration emergency overrides tied to SLO alerts and on-call approvals; add emergency reserve pool for rapid burst scaling.
Add composite observability dashboard linking routing shifts, cache-fill progress, autoscaler activity, and per-replica queue lengths for faster diagnosis.

Post-release monitoring: run 72-hour canary after runtime-1.24 with stress tests that simulate simultaneous region failovers.
review_feedback: Elena Cho (SRE Manager): Add explicit service-level tests for prewarm correctness and failures during partial prewarm.

verification_plan: Unit + integration tests for coordinated CB consensus steps merged to main and gated by CI.
Chaos test: simulate control-plane leader churn + immediate traffic shift; require no SLO breach in staging for 3 consecutive runs.
Canary rollout of cache prewarm and autoscaler override to 5% of clusters with real traffic, monitor composite dashboard for 72 hours.
notes: Trade-offs considered: stricter circuit-breaker lockstep reduces risk of partial overloads but may increase blast radius during config errors; chosen plan favors consensus with manual override path.
Short term manual widening of CB thresholds had potential to mask downstream problems; action items focus on deterministic transitions rather than permanent widening.
This incident highlighted an observability blind spot; dashboards and alerting must make cross-service warmup progress visible within 30s of failover initiation.
